alkylation_reagent.evidence: Tumor tissue from breast cancer biopsies homogenized with a glass glass homogenizer; isolation of the cytoplasmic protein fraction; SDS-PAGE separation of proteins; in gel digest of eight slices with trypsin including reduction of cysteins with DTT and alkylation with IAA; separation of peptides with nano-LC (Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano) using a 2cm C-18 trapping column with 100µm diameter and 5µm particle size and a 15cm C-18 separation column with 75µm diameter and 2µm particle size; peptides were eluted with a flow rate of 300nl/min from the pre-column to the analytical column and separated with a gradient of 1% to 40% mobile phase B (20% H2O, 80% ACN, 0.2% FA) over 45min; identification of peptides using a Thermo QExactive orbitrap mass spectrometer at a resolution of 40 000 (at m/z=200) for MS1 followed by MS/MS scans of the six most abundant ions upon fragmentation in the HCD cell at 30% normalized collision energy (isolation width of Δm/z = 2, resolution 17500 at m/z = 200).
